{{Recipe}}

Also called '''common meringue''', '''French meringue''' is a simple [[Cookbook:Meringue|meringue]] made by whipping egg whites and beating in granulated sugar. It can be baked into cookies or a crispy base for pavlova, vacherin, or other desserts.

== Ingredients ==

* 8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (250 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Egg White|egg whites]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Cream of Tartar|cream of tartar]] or a few drops [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]]
* 8 oz (250 g) [[Cookbook:Granulated Sugar|granulated sugar]]
* 8 oz (250 g) [[Cookbook:Superfine Sugar|superfine sugar]] or sifted [[Cookbook:Powdered Sugar|confectioners' sugar]]

== Preparation ==

# [[Cookbook:Whipping|Whip]] the egg whites and cream of tartar until they reach soft peaks.
# Add the first amount of sugar, little by little, while beating by hand or machine.
# Whip until stiff.
# Stop beating and fold in the remaining sugar, if used, with a spatula.
# Use as desired or in your recipe.
